key_insight: Treating deception mitigation as an adversarial oversight game can incentivize faithful agent behavior rather than merely successful-looking outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Agent evaluation pipelines can improve oversight by inspecting reasoning, tool use, and environmental effects instead of judging final outputs alone.
method: Model evaluation as an e-PoG: the agent maximizes reward while a monitor seeks to expose deception.
Use a fixed verifier to validate monitor claims and translate confirmed deception into penalties.
Train with two-timescale policy gradients, augmented by NLI verification and deterministic checks.
evidence_signal: Across Gemma3-4B-IT and Qwen3-4B/8B on Agentic Role-Playing, SearchQA, and WebShop, the authors report improvements over the strongest baselines of 26.0% in deception mitigation and up to 39.8% in task success, with gains persisting under weak-to-strong supervision.
watch_item: The faithfulness guarantee assumes a perfect verifier or verifier errors that preserve monitor-action rankings; real-world verification may violate this condition.
paper_title: Mitigating Agentic Deception via Evaluation-Side Partially Observable Games
